title: Allisha Gray injury: Dream star 'making progress,' status for WNBA Finals unclear - CBS Sports
description: Atlanta's title chances may hinge on Gray's availability vs. Golden State
body:
Atlanta's title chances may hinge on Gray's availability vs. Golden State
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        OAKLAND, Calif. -- When the doors at the Sephora Performance Center opened on Friday morning, and media were allowed into the gym to watch the end of the Atlanta Dream's last practice ahead of the 2026 WNBA Finals, star guard Allisha Gray was running through a full-court drill with the starters. While that was a positive sign, Gray's status for Game 1 against the Golden State Valkyries on Saturday remains uncertain due to a hand injury she suffered in the semifinals. Gray, whose 19 points per game led the Dream in scoring and ranked ninth in the league, said after practice that she's still "day-to-day." Dream coach Karl Smesko said a decision on whether Gray will suit up will be made close to tip-off, which is set for 3:30 p.m. ET at Chase Center. "My hand feels good. Today in practice was really my first day of actually being able to have a full practice, go through contact and stuff like that," Gray said. "Right now I'm still day-to-day and then we're gonna see how my finger reacts to how practice went today and we'll see tomorrow."Gray, who still had the pinky and ring fingers on her left shooting hand taped together, said she doesn't think about her finger when she's on the court, and was "just so happy" to be able to "run up and down the court and be able to shoot." She added that the medical staff will ultimately make the final call on whether she'll play. 
"I think she's looking good, making progress," Smesko said. "I don't need to see anything from her. If she's able to go, we'd love for her to go."
Gray recently underwent a "minor" procedure on her left hand after she injured it during Game 1 of the semifinals against the New York Liberty. Specifics regarding her injury and the timing and extent of the procedure remain unclear. Early in that contest in Brooklyn, she deflected a pass from Sabrina Ionescu. After a short trip to the locker room, Gray returned to the game with tape on her fingers. Her first shot was a bad miss from 3-point range, so she removed the tape. In the second quarter, she made another nice defensive play on Ionescu, but aggravated the injury in the process and has not played since. 
Despite Gray's absence, the Dream swept the Liberty in three games to advance to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. 
Dream's title chances may hinge on Gray's availability"Allisha's one of the best players in the W," Dream coach Karl Smesko said Tuesday. "To advance and beat a great New York team basically without her, except for 10 minutes of one game, is a testament to everybody else raising their game. But it would be great to have her back for the Finals. She's just somebody that, offensively, is really hard to stop, and then she makes defensive plays. She's just an all-around great player."
        
            
                2026 WNBA playoffs bracket: WNBA Finals schedule tweaked so Dream can use larger venue
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Dream's ability to beat the Valkyries and win the first championship in franchise history may hinge on Gray's availability. Jordin Canada, DeWanna Bonner and Isobel Borlase were spectacular in the semifinals against the Liberty, but it's a big ask for them to repeat these performances:
Canada had three of the five-highest playoff scoring performances of her career against the Liberty, and averaged 22.3 points on 62.2/61.5/100 shooting splits -- up from 11.6 points on 43.1/29.2/78.2 shooting in the regular season. Bonner went for 15.3 points and 8.3 rebounds on 50/46.7/80 shooting splits, up from 10.4 points and six rebounds on 40.2/27.9/84.3 shooting between the Phoenix Mercury and Dream in the regular season. And Borlase, who only had six double-digit scoring games in the regular season, came off the bench to chip in 11 points in Game 2 and 10 points in Game 3 while shooting 9 of 15, including 3 of 6 from 3-point range. The Valkyries have the best defense in the league by a wide margin, and just shut down A'ja Wilson and Jackie Young in a sweep of the Las Vegas Aces. Even acknowledging the Valkyries' own issues on offense, it's hard to imagine how the Dream would be able to score enough points to beat them without Gray. While Gray will clearly not be 100% if she suits up, having an All-WNBA-caliber talent on the floor that the Valkyries have to respect would make life far easier for the Dream.

title: DeWanna Bonner could be the WNBA Finals' biggest X-Factor -- and she took an unlikely path to the Dream - CBS Sports
description: The veteran joined Atlanta just two months ago and is now one of the biggest reasons why the Dream are in the Fin
body:
The veteran joined Atlanta just two months ago and is now one of the biggest reasons why the Dream are in the Finals
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:23 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        SAN FRANCISCO -- Less than two months ago, on Aug. 22, DeWanna Bonner scored 12 points and grabbed nine rebounds for the Phoenix Mercury in a 10-point loss to the Atlanta Dream. By then, the Mercury had long since become the first team since 2008 to miss the playoffs in the season following a Finals appearance. And what may be the final season of the 39-year-old Bonner's storied career was nearing a depressing end. Until, two days later, when the Mercury released Bonner just before the deadline for player playoff eligibility from waivers. Three days after that, on Aug. 27, Bonner signed with the Dream for the remainder of the season. "It happened that Phoenix and her worked out a deal to allow her to make a run in the postseason and that turned into a mini-free agency with a bunch of teams that went after her," Dream general manager Dan Padover said earlier this month. "We were fortunate that we had made a run at her the last few free agencies. She has a great relationship with our players, which helped."Padover took over the Dream's basketball operations in 2022, and over the last four years made five separate trades to acquire all five members of Atlanta's starting lineup: Jordin Canada, Allisha Gray, Rhyne Howard, Naz Hillmon and Angel Reese. That's three All-Stars, last season's Sixth Player of the Year, this season's Defensive Player of the Year and three All-Defensive honorees. 

        
            
                From stunning Angel Reese trade to expansion ingenuity: How Dream, Valkyries broke the mold to reach Finals
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
And yet, without Bonner falling in their lap, the Dream might not be in the Finals for the first time since 2013. "I think she's made a difference both in terms of how good a player she is. She contributes to winning every time she's out there. And I think she has everybody's attention," Dream coach Karl Smesko said Friday after the team's last pre-Finals practice. "She has the right thing to say at the right moment. She's just been a great addition for us as a player and as a leader."
Now in her 17th season, Bonner has won two championships and is the only player in WNBA history to surpass 100 postseason appearances. "She's played more playoff games than I have regular-season games," Dream rookie Isobel Borlase joked. That's underselling it. Bonner's 103 playoff games are more than double Borlase's 44 career games. When Bonner made her debut back in 2009, Borlase wasn't even 5 years old. 
"It's experience, and you can't buy it," Borlase said. "I think the biggest thing for us in the locker room is just her voice. She's a calming voice but also a motivator. She knows when to tell us to pull it together and when to calm down." The rest of the Dream roster had a combined 120 playoff appearances entering this postseason, and Canada and Shatori Walker-Kimbrough, who isn't in the rotation, are the only other players with a ring. "She knows what it takes to win a championship," Gray said. "When DB speaks, you listen." Reese added that Bonner has kept the team "humble" and "grounded," and "told us how important every little detail is gonna be." Bonner, for her part, said that the biggest lesson she's tried to impart is the importance of staying "even keel," especially in a seven-game series. (The Finals were expanded to best-of-seven last season.) "You gotta manage yourself, you gotta manage your emotions, you gotta manage your body," Bonner said. 
Of course, all Bonner's intangibles would mean little without production, and she's playing her best basketball of the season in the playoffs.In Game 1 of the first round against the Washington Mystics, Bonner took over the third quarter to turn an 11-point deficit into 15-point win, and the Dream have never looked back. Bonner has scored in double figures in four of the Dream's five playoff games and put up 23 points in Game 1 of the semifinals against the New York Liberty after Gray went down with a hand injury. She then stepped into the starting lineup for the remainder of the semis and recorded the 20th double-double of her playoff career in the series-clinching Game 3 win. Just look at the splits between Bonner's regular-season numbers and her playoff numbers.

Season10.461.61.140.227.9Playoffs13.26.41.6144.936.8Bonner credited her teammates for making it "easy" for her to come in and assume a leadership role so late in the season. "They accepted it. They're teaching me a lot at the same time," Bonner said. "I'm coming into a team that they've been playing this way all season, so I'm learning as well. We just switch off. They give me a lot of in-game experience and I'm giving them a little bit of knowledge."Together, they could give Atlanta its first ever WNBA championship.

title: Texas Tech QB Thomas Castellanos ruled eligible after judge grants injunction against NCAA - CBS Sports
description: Castellanos missed Texas Tech's game against Colorado after being ruled ineligible, but he'll be available on Sat
body:
Castellanos missed Texas Tech's game against Colorado after being ruled ineligible, but he'll be available on Saturday against Arizona State
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:28 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Texas Tech quarterback Thomas Castellanos is once again eligible after a Jefferson Circuit Court judge granted him an injunction against the NCAA. He will now be available for the Red Raiders' game against Arizona State on Saturday.Before the season, a judge granted Castellanos a temporary restraining order that allowed him to return for a fifth year of eligibility. The former Florida State quarterback committed to Texas Tech and saw limited action in the first four games of the season.Recently, a Kentucky judge dissolved the temporary restraining order that gave Castellanos his extra year of eligibility, making him ineligible right before the Red Raiders' Week 5 win over Colorado.With Castellanos back in the fold, Texas Tech will have improved depth and mobility at the quarterback position. Castellanos has attempted just four passes for the Red Raiders, but he's rushed 10 times for 44 yards and two touchdowns. That should give the Sun Devils' defense something else to think about this weekend.
That's assuming, of course, that Castellanos will be limited to a more gadget role. Based on how starter Will Hammond has performed this season, Castellanos could get an extended look if the Red Raiders offense struggles early against Arizona State.QB competition in Lubbock?It's been a shaky start to the season for Hammond, who has struggled mightily at times.Against Sam Houston State, Hammond completed just 58.6 percent of his passes for one touchdown and three interceptions. Against a lackluster Colorado defense, Hammond and the offense were stuck in neutral for most of the game. The Buffaloes led well into the third quarter, until the Red Raiders finally broke through for their first touchdown.
With Hammond at the helm, Texas Tech is averaging just 406.4 yards per game, which ranks 12th in the Big 12. The Red Raiders also average a pedestrian 34.8 points per game, which sits eighth in the conference.Castellanos brings another element to the offense with his legs, and he now has 42 games of experience under his belt. Castellanos can be loose with the football at times, but Hammond hasn't exactly taken care of the football with five picks in as many games.Despite Hammond leading an uninspiring offense, Texas Tech remains undefeated and inside the top 10 of the AP Top 25 poll. However, if Hammond continues to struggle against tougher competition, would Joey McGuire contemplate a switch to Castellanos?

title: Josh Jacobs, Jonathon Cooper to be removed from NFL exempt list, eligible for Week 7 return - CBS Sports
description: Both players will become eligible for Week 7, although their teams must determine whether they are ready to play
body:
Both players will become eligible for Week 7, although their teams must determine whether they are ready to play
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The league announced two players will be removed from the NFL's Commissioner Exempt list in the coming days. Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper will be removed on Friday, and Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs on Monday.Cooper is eligible to play in Denver's Week 7 game against the Arizona Cardinals, and Jacobs is expected to be eligible to play in Green Bay's Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions, according to ESPN. "The league's review of both the Josh Jacobs and Jonathon Cooper situations 'remains ongoing' and is not affected by the change to either player's status," the report states. Players on the commissioner's exempt list continue to be paid. If the NFL later suspends either player, the league could credit the games missed on the exempt list toward the suspension and seek repayment of salary earned during that period. Being on the list means players cannot attend practice or games. 
Cooper was dismissed from minicamp and was placed on the list ahead of the season following two arrests involving an alleged domestic violence incident with his ex-girlfriend in June. He faces five charges, including second-degree felony assault. His trial was moved from mid-November to early March.Cooper has spent his entire career thus far with the Broncos, who drafted him in the seventh round of the 2021 NFL Draft. Jacobs was charged with two misdemeanors, battery and damage to property, from an arrest in May. Jacobs filed an action seeking to prevent the public release of evidence related to the case, including alleged video of the incident. Jacobs' attorney released a statement saying he "accepts responsibility for his actions" and says he is "excited to get back on the field with his teammates."
Jacobs signed a four-year, $48 million deal with the Packers heading into the 2024 season and he is now in his third year with the team. The All-Pro was selected by the Las Vegas Raiders at No. 24 overall in the 2019 NFL Draft.In his absence, RB Marshawn Lloyd has led the team with just 112 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Kaleb Johnson is second on the team with 106 yards. While both players will be eligible to return in Week 7, that decision is ultimately up to the coaches and players involved.

title: Washington QB Demond Williams Jr. to miss game vs. Purdue with rib injury - CBS Sports
description: Junior backup signal caller Elijah Brown will get the start for the Huskies as they look to correct their offenis
body:
Junior backup signal caller Elijah Brown will get the start for the Huskies as they look to correct their offenisve woes against the Boilermakers
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With star quarterback Demond Williams Jr. sidelined with a rib injury, junior Elijah Brown will start for Washington against Purdue on Friday night.It's already been a tough season for the Huskies, but this development won't make it any easier. Washington is still looking for its first win in Big Ten play, and that task just got a little more difficult.Brown, a former four-star recruit out of California, played the first two seasons of his career at Stanford before transferring to Washington in the offseason. Brown saw a little action at Stanford and started in a couple of games last season, most notably in a win over Cal and a loss to North Carolina.In nine career appearances with the Cardinal, Brown completed 58.3 percent of his passes for 1,103 yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions. Brown has played in mop-up duty a few times in his first season at Washington, resulting in 276 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions on 71.4 percent passing.
Washington needs Brown to spark the passing game because that's been the only way the offense has moved the ball this season. The Huskies rank 16th in the Big Ten with 26.2 points per game, and a pitiful run game has a lot to do with that.Bad news for a struggling offenseAlthough Williams has been somewhat disappointing in 2026, he's still done enough to make plays and put the ball in the end zone on a number of occasions. In other words, Williams has found a way to make it work here and there.The same can't be said for the running game, which has been anemic. The Huskies average just 90.3 rushing yards per game, which ranks 135th out of 138 teams nationall. They also rank 106th in yards per rush (4.06) and rushing success rate (39.7 percent).
That's a bad recipe for a team starting an unproven quarterback on the road in conference play, although there is some hope that Brown has what it takes to lead the offense efficiently.After Williams got hurt against Iowa last week, Brown relatively well in relief. In fact, he started the second half 14-of-16 while leading two straight touchdown drives against the Hawkeyes defense."Just trusting in the process," Brown said of his performance against Iowa. "Just trusting in the coach's plans. I feel like they prepared us very well. That's pretty much it."
Perhaps Brown has taken big strides in his first year at Washington. That would be great, but what if he hasn't? Didn't Dylan Raiola look great against USC when he took over for an injured Dante Moore. One week later, he was benched against UCLA.If Brown does struggle, Washington will go from one-dimensional to zero-dimensional on offense, and even a subpar defense like Purdue's could slow down the Huskies. In that case, Jedd Fisch and and his team would be on their way to a 3-4 record while remaining winless in Big Ten play.

title: Spirit vs. Gotham live stream: Where to watch NWSL rivalry showdown online - CBS Sports
description: First place and a potential NWSL Shield clinch are on the line at Audi Field, while Washington fight to lock down
body:
First place and a potential NWSL Shield clinch are on the line at Audi Field, while Washington fight to lock down a playoff spot in the latest chapter of their fierce rivalry
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:37 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It's the best time of the year in NWSL, the playoff push. With just a few games left in the 2026 regular season and the NWSL Shield still up for grabs, every game from here on out feels like a must-win. But, add rivalry to the mix, and the stakes get a little higher.Every great rivalry has iconic moments, and Gotham FC and Washington Spirit have already racked up several in recent years. Washington Spirit won a triumphant penalty shootout at Audi Field in the 2024 NWSL semifinals, and Gotham FC won last year's NWSL Championship game.Earlier this season, Gotham took home bragging rights with a narrow 1-0 win for the first-ever victory at MLB's Citi Field in front of 42,175 fans.
The two teams will meet in a final regular-season fixture, just weeks before the NWSL playoffs begin. But both sides have stakes in the match. Gotham FC already claimed a postseason spot, are in first place, are leading the NWSL Shield race, and can potentially lift the shield. Meanwhile, the Spirit are in third place, still in contention for the shield, and chasing a playoff clinch.
However, both rosters face uncertainty ahead of the game. Injury concerns and cohesion struggles loom, and with the playoffs so close, gamesmanship could flare in a rivalry that's already typically cagey.How to watch Washington Spirit vs. Gotham FC, oddsDate: Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time: 12:30 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS Odds: Washington Spirit +160; Draw +230; NJ/NJ Gotham +155Injury concerns for Gotham FCGotham FC have been on an impressive run of form since the league returned following a summer break for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, with only two losses since July 4. With an unbeaten run through August and more wins in September, the East Coast club has held on firmly to first place. 
Equally impressive has been the club's ability to navigate changes across the sidelines and the roster. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros and his family welcomed a new baby, and he took parental leave back in July."I'm incredibly grateful to everyone at Gotham FC for supporting us unconditionally while we were deciding to take this step," Amoros said in the summer. "This is a personal decision for our family, but I also recognize the visibility that comes with my role. When fathers take parental leave, particularly men in leadership positions, it helps normalize an important principle: Caring for children is a shared responsibility between parents. I need to be there for my family."Between then-acting head coach Shaun Harris and Amoros, the club's record was ten wins, three draws, and two losses through September, and they also had to manage the roster as injuries piled up, with a season-ending torn patellar tendon for Emily Sonnett and a brief concussion precaution for Rose Lavelle. 
The injury list is still growing ahead of Saturday's big game. Rookie Jordynn Dudley's impressive campaign was cut short with a foot fracture, and while on international duty, Brazilian defender Brunhina tore her ACL. Both players are on the season-ending injury list ahead of the weekend. Jaedyn Shaw was recently called up to join USWNT camps with the U23 side, though she was sent home early as a precaution following a minor injury. She is currently day-to-day and expected to be available for Saturday's game against the Spirit.The recent international window may have added minutes for players on national teams; it may have come at a good time for others ahead of a potential NWSL Shield clinch scenario. One of Gotham's strengths this season has been a deep bench that has played together for a few seasons, while rookies stepped up and new additions like Australian international Sam Kerr have slotted in fairly seamlessly following the departure of Esther Gonzalez.
The recent acquisition of Spain defender Leila Ouahabi could mean another tactical shift for Midge Purce, who could play more of an attacking role along the front line, while Ouahabi shifts into a natural position at outside back.Cohesion struggles for Washington SpiritThe Spirit's second half of the season has been more split than Gotham. With eight wins, six losses, and one draw since July, the group has struggled to keep pace for the NWSL Shield, but looks primed for another postseason appearance. Inconsistency in results isn't uncommon in a long NWSL season, and the Spirit shook off a four-game winless streak in August to finally pick up a trio of wins across five matches in September. Roster churn could also help explain some of the unevenness.
Beyond preseason movement, including key midfield departures Croix Bethune (Kansas City Current) and Narumi Miura (Utah Royals) to other playoff-contending teams at the start of the season, the club has made plenty of mid- to late-season roster shakeups. Cameroonian midfielder Monique Ngock and Algerian midfielder Mélissa Bethi joined after the Women's Africa Cup of Nations, and the club recently signed Tanzanian national team forward Clara Luvanga. Mexico international Rebecal Bernal, with 20 appearances for the Spirit this season, joined Manchester United in September. Losing a regular from the squad in the middle of a Shield chase left little time for the defense or midfield to readjust, especially with Leicy Santos out for an extended injury absence. Though there might finally be some light at the end of the long absence tunnel.
Both Andi Sullivan and Ashley Hatch returned to the roster following maternity leave midseason and earned match minutes, and head coach Adrian Gonzalez said in a recent pregame press conference that Santos will be available for selection against Gotham.It's a sign that maybe the international break arrived at a good time for the club's recent signings and injured players. The franchise is investing in international talent, and that's positive for the present and future, but chemistry rarely arrives the moment a new deal is signed. Now that everyone has had a handful of games to get acclimated and a brief international break in the schedule, the Spirit can look ahead to managing the three games remaining in front of them, but first is a high-stakes game against Gotham.What's at stakeThere's plenty to play for on Saturday. Gotham is chasing a prize it has never won. With two NWSL Championships, a Concacaf title, and a recent NWSL Challenge Cup, the title of best team in the league has eluded them. They have a chance to hoist the Shield with a road win over one of their oldest rivals, with help from a North Carolina Courage win.
"There's not a lot of direct talk about it because we all understand that what we're doing every day and every week is what leads to that. So while it's an ultimate goal that we've set from the beginning of preseason, we have a good understanding that thinking about that goal is not necessarily what's going to get you there. It's what you're doing every day at training; it's what you're doing on the weekend playing these games," said Gotham defender Tierna Davidson before the international break."That's really what we're focused on, knowing in the back of our minds that that's what we're working towards together. I also think too, sometimes if you talk about something too much, you forget what's right in front of you. And that's important that we continue to focus on what's in front of us ... ultimately, as a team, we understand that there are short-term goals, midterm goals, long-term goals, but we can accomplish all of that together without having to compromise in any way," she said.The Spirit have the math on their side in the Shield race, but they must beat Gotham and win their remaining games (nine points) to have a shot.
Beyond the shield, there is playoff positioning on the line for both sides. Even if Gotham stumble in their remaining games, the pride of playing for a home playoff is there. Teams that place first through fourth could potentially host up to two home games. Gotham has already clinched a postseason spot, and the Spirit can also cement another postseason berth with a win, or help from positive results by San Diego, Bay FC, or Chicago.

title: Florida trending toward starting Tramell Jones at QB vs. Texas as Aaron Philo deals with injury - CBS Sports
description: The Gators appear ready to turn to their young QB on the road against the Longhorns on Saturday
body:
The Gators appear ready to turn to their young QB on the road against the Longhorns on Saturday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:34 pm ET

        Although Florida quarterback Aaron Philo has been classified as a game-time decision against No. 7 Texas, it's trending toward sophomore Tramell Jones Jr. making his first career start, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.Philo was injured in the Gators' 38-19 loss to South Carolina last week, and Jones struggled in relief. The sophomore threw for 40 yards and one interception while completing six of his eight pass attempts.That lackluster showing against the Gamecocks aside, Jones has the potential to be a tremendous playmaker for Florida. He was a three-star recruit and the No. 25 quarterback in the 2025 signing class, per 247Sports. Andrew Ivins, the 247Sports Director of Scouting, even compared Jones to Florida legend Chris Leak.Jones received some first-team reps at practice throughout the week, under the assumption that Philo would be unable to play. Coach Jon Sumrall said he was pleased with how Jones responded.
"They're both working hard every day, and Tramell is gonna be ready when his number is called, and he's gonna continue to have opportunities as we move forward," Sumrall said, per 247Sports."I love the way [Jones has] handled himself. Tramell's been great. Philo's been great. At practice today, one of my favorite moments at practice: We're doing some routes-on-air stuff, and, Philo's standing right next to Tramell and Tramell makes a throw and Philo's like, '9, what a great ball. Let's go.' They're there for each other."When Philo followed offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner from Georgia Tech, the assumption was that he would be locked in as the starting quarterback. Philo won the job, but Jones pushed the competition into fall camp after flashing at times in spring practice.
Tough first testIf Florida has its ideal scenario, Jones wouldn't be making his first career start on the road against Texas, which boasts one of the best defenses in the country. The Longhorns have been relentless on that side of the ball, and the numbers show it.They rank 12th nationally in yards allowed per game (264.4), 21st nationally in points allowed per game (16.0), sixth in EPA per play and 15th in success rate (37.9 percent)Yards allowed per game264.4 (12th)Points allowed per game16.0 (21st)EPA per play-0.16 (6th)Success rate37.9% (15th)It all starts up front with Colin Simmons, a future first-round NFL draft pick who leads the country in tackles for loss (12) and sacks (9.5). He has plenty of help in the front seven, thanks to defensive lineman Hero Kanu and linebacker Rasheem Biles.In the secondary, cornerbacks Graceson Littleton and Bo Mascoe can capitalize on any mistake Jones makes if he finds himself under pressure.We've already seen what Texas can do to an inexperienced quarterback once this season. Against Tennessee, the Longhorns sacked Faizon Brandon 10 times and forced two fumbles, although the Volunteers fell on both of them. In that game, Brandon had the advantage of operating the offense at home, a luxury Jones won't have in Darrell K Royal on Saturday.The Gators do have a star running back who could take some heat off Jones, Jadan Baugh, but he's been neutralized in two consecutive games. Florida has to find a way to create more running room for him against a stout Texas front.

description: A pair of title fights headline this weekend's action in both England and the U.S.

A pair of title fights headline this weekend's action in both England and the U.S.

        In May, Daniel Dubois won the WBO heavyweight championship with a stoppage win over Fabio Wardley. On Saturday, the pair will run it back in London (2 p.m. ET, DAZN PPV). That rematch highlights boxing's weekend schedule, though it's not the only world title fight on the menu.In the first meeting between Dubois and Wardley, Wardley scored knockdowns of Dubois in the first and third rounds. Despite that early success, the real story of the fight was the toughness Wardley showed across the rest of the fight, absorbing a tremendous beating from Dubois.Dubois was able to take advantage of Wardley's limited offensive approach and land crushing right hands round after round. All Wardley could do in response was go back to the well with the same looping one-two combinations that had produced the earlier knockdowns.
Wardley started boxing late in life, competing in white-collar shows from age 21 before turning professional. He found plenty of success, including late comeback knockout wins over Justis Huni and Joseph Parker in interim title fights before being promoted to full champion ahead of the Dubois fight.
Dubois came up in a more traditional fashion, working through the amateurs before turning pro. That seasoning provided the skills and knowledge that allowed Dubois to make further adjustments and become a more dynamic fighter after he tasted Wardley's power early on.Dubois has three losses in his career, all by knockout, including a pair to Oleksandr Usyk. Beyond those losses, Dubois has picked up many big wins, including over Anthony Joshua in a British megafight in 2024.Prediction: There's no reason to think the rematch plays out much differently than the first bout. That is especially true with the rematch coming so shortly after the first meeting. As mentioned, Wardley took a hellacious beating in that fight, and since then he has had to recover as much as possible and hasn't had much time to add new wrinkles to his game. Dubois is the better fighter, and as long as he can avoid a pure knockout shot, he should be able to put a hurting on Wardley again. Pick: Daniel Dubois via TKO7
Sebastian Fundora vs. Ermal HadribeajThe other big fight on Saturday takes place in Las Vegas, where Sebastian Fundora will defend his WBC junior middleweight title against Ermal Hadribeaj (8 p.m. ET, DAZN).Fundora has developed into a really good fighter after starting his career seen by many as a sideshow, with his 6-foot-6 frame towering over opponents, but a tendency to fight toe-to-toe rather than at a range that best utilized his reach. As things seemed to have been moving in the right direction, Fundora suffered a shocking knockout loss to Brian Mendoza.Fundora rebounded from the Mendoza loss with a split-decision win over Tim Tszyu that was largely attributed to Tszyu suffering a nasty cut early in the fight as a result of a Fundora elbow. Fundora erased all doubt about that win two fights later, stopping Tszyu just seven rounds into the fight.
In his most recent fight, Fundora took just six rounds to stop Keith Thurman in their March bout.Hadribeaj isn't a big-name fighter, and Fundora is far and away the best opponent he will have faced, but at 23-0-1, Hadribeaj has yet to suffer a loss. His most recent fight was a career-best win, taking a decision win over previously undefeated Bakary Samake.That said, Hadribeaj has only scored eight knockouts in his career, so he likely doesn't have the power to keep Fundora off of him as the fight wears on.
Prediction: This is set up to be little more than a showcase for Fundora. He has the better resume and the kind of physical tools that simply can't be taught. Now that Fundora better mixes in fighting at distance with his ability to stand and trade inside, he's a very big problem for the junior middleweight division. Hadribeaj doesn't figure to be the fighter who can take the belt from Fundora's waist.

title: Jaylen Waddle trade revisited: Bo Nix, Broncos struggling to integrate speedy WR - CBS Sports
description: Neither the Denver passing offense nor Waddle are playing well
body:
Neither the Denver passing offense nor Waddle are playing well
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In Bo Nix's preseason debut this year -- his first football game since breaking his ankle -- he rifled a ball to Jaylen Waddle, who had won on a vertical route up the middle of the field. Waddle caught it and sped away from his defender, a 35-yard gain. The Denver crowd erupted, even for a preseason game. This is what they had wanted so badly, the missing piece for a team that was on the doorstep of a Super Bowl berth last year.
Denver needed explosiveness. Waddle brought it in bunches. This was the start of a beautiful marriage.Or, maybe not.After another eyesore offensive performance from Denver in which Waddle was hardly involved (four catches, 24 yards), we revisit the deal this offseason that came with seemingly so much promise ... and wonder if Waddle and Nix can get on track.The tradeBroncos receive: WR Jaylen Waddle, 2026 fourth-round pick (T Kage Casey)Dolphins receive: 2026 first-round pick (used in trade up to draft CB Chris Johnson), 2026 third-round pick (WR Chris Bell), 2026 fourth-round pick (EDGE Trey Moore)The Dolphins were in the midst of a massive teardown that included the release of Tyreek Hill, Tua Tagovailoa and Bradley Chubb. Miami, 27, was neither as old as Hill or Chubb nor as costly as Tagovailoa, but Miami opted to wipe the slate as clean as possible, and Denver seemed to be the perfect home.
Denver ranked 27th in average depth of target when throwing to wide receivers last year (7.4 yards). Waddle was at 13.1.Waddle averaged 14.1 yards per catch last year; only one Denver wide receiver, Courtland Sutton was over 11.Adding the speed and explosiveness of Waddle to a group that included a big-bodied possession receiver (Sutton) and several ancillary pieces was going to unlock Nix, the Broncos thought.Bo Nix not helping Jaylen Waddle, Jaylen Waddle not helping himselfThe supposed "perfect combination" has actually been, for the most part early this season, very little combination. Through six games, Waddle has 22 catches for 228 yards and one touchdown. His 10.4 yards per reception are on pace to be his worst number since his rookie year.Jaylen Waddle this seasonOn pace for career worst?Receptions per game3.67YesReceiving yards per game38YesFirst down rate41%YesCatch rate58%YesWaddle has played a large role in that last line. He has four drops already this season after three all of last year. He came to Denver with a 6.1% career drop rate (which already wasn't great), but he is at a very bad 10.8% this year.The preseason wasn't the only false hope. After a brutal Week 1 in which pretty much everything went wrong for Denver, Waddle caught eight of 10 targets for 138 yards against the Jaguars, showing off his full skill set. He caught a 49-yarder downfield. He made catches on in-breaking routes, something he did so well in Miami. He showed off his YAC ability, and he absolutely roasted Jourdan Lewis for a crucial third-down conversion. Sean Payton talked up the need to get him the football. It seemed like all was on track.
Outside of the Jaguars game, Waddle's longest catch is 13 yards. Three of his five targets 20+ yards downfield came in the Jaguars game; the other two are an underthrow and a near-interception into double coverage. And the frustration spilled over in Week 5, when Nix checked into a run play on third and long.
Nix's passing tendencies have bordered on playing not to lose, rather than playing to win. His average throw travels 4.9 yards downfield, not only the shortest in the NFL this season but also the shortest by any quarterback through six games in the last 20 years. He simply is not even attempting to hit Waddle in the intermediate and deep areas where Waddle thrives.Furthermore, it's not as if Waddle hasn't been open. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Waddle has an average separation of 3.9 yards, the 11th-highest rate in the league and much higher than his mark last year (2.7).Remember all those fun downfield routes Waddle got against the Jaguars? Here's what his seven targeted routes looked like Thursday.
Of course, this was on a short week and just the second week since Sean Payton took playcalling duties back from Davis Webb. But there is a clear disconnect between what Waddle provides, what Nix wants to throw and what the coaching staff trusts Nix to do. One clip going around is Nix opting against firing a downfield throw to Waddle to instead throw a dump-off that gets knocked down. Like in Week 4, Waddle is not happy after the play.
It's not like the work is being funneled elsewhere. The entire passing attack is bad. Waddle leads all Broncos with 228 receiving yards and is nearly 100 yards ahead of the next-closest wide receiver (Pat Bryant, 133).At some point, Nix has to push the ball downfield. It will take a combination of his willingness and the staff scheming more downfield throws Nix is comfortable with -- his comfort level is clearly very low right now -- but this isn't close to the Waddle anyone expected. There's blame to share.It's also not worth writing off 100%. Waddle's drops are at a career-worst rate. Nix's downfield throwing is at a career-worst rate. We'd like to see more chances for Waddle on in-breaking routes -- he has just four receptions on ins, crossers, slants and posts -- and a greater willingness for Nix to throw them. The play-calling has been mixed, and Nix still doesn't look like himself. Maybe more time removed from the ankle injury, which sapped much of his offseason, will help. It's been concerning, but the season is only one-third of the way done.Too early to know about Dolphins' returnJust like it's early for Denver, it's early for Miami. In the grand scheme, it's much, much earlier, even. The Dolphins aren't likely to contend for ... a while. Assessing how they did in this trade will take ... a while.Miami and its youngsters are taking their lumps this season, as expected, but they have shown some good signs. Chris Johnson is PFF's No. 21-graded cornerback, just behind some bigger names such as Devon Witherspoon, Quinyon Mitchell and Travis Hunter.Johnson's 6.1 yards per attempt allowed as primary defender ranks 24th out of 74 defensive backs targeted at least 20 times, and his 8.6 yards per completion allowed is 11th. There is a lot to like here.It's even earlier for Chris Bell, an explosive wide receiver with borderline first-round talent who fell to the third round after a torn ACL. He has just five catches on 16 routes, but those five catches have gone for 92 yards. Again, patience is required.
Moore unfortunately suffered an ankle injury in the preseason and had to undergo surgery. He is still on IR.

Notably, 'under' parlays on the same player's statistics are off the board
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the aftermath of multiple high-profile gambling scandals, the NBA will no longer allow certain types of bets that would appear to be the lowest-hanging fruit for potential conspirators. Citing a memo distributed to the league's sportsbook partners on Friday, ESPN is reporting that "bettors will not be able to include the under on the same player's statistics in parlays, in addition to other betting markets the league considers problematic."
From ESPN: The league also directed its authorized gambling operators, including DraftKings and FanDuel, not to offer bets on the winner of the opening tip, players to miss specific shots and under bets on players who are expected to play fewer than 12 minutes in a specific game.The NBA has the authority to restrict what partner sportsbooks offer through its agreements. The NBA estimates its partner sportsbooks account for upward of 99% of the U.S. betting market.These bets on an individual player's over/under lines are particularly ripe for fixing because the player can control the outcome. These were the bets exploited by Jontay Porter, who received a lifetime ban in 2024 for disclosing inside information to bettors and wagering on games. Porter admitted in court that he took himself out of games early to make sure his under bets hit. 
If you're not familiar with how these lines work, let's say a player's rebounding line for a game is set at 3.5. If you bet the under, you are betting that the player will finish with three or fewer rebounds. Obviously, a player can largely control that by simply not pursuing rebounds, and he can eliminate the possibility of even accidentally running into a loose rebound or two by simply removing himself from the game for a fake injury once he has logged the time to make the game and bets on his lines official. He relays this information to bettors beforehand, and they put a bunch of money on him to go under the projected total. ESPN notes that in the Porter criminal complaint, federal prosecutors pointed to one bettor placing an $80,000 parlay bet on Porter going under his line for assists, rebounds, points, 3-pointers, steals and blocks for a March 2024 game between the Raptors and Kings that stood to pay out more than a million dollars. Porter left that game after playing just three minutes. The same type of scandal has been alleged involving Terry Rozier, who removed himself after playing just nine minutes in a 2023 game that was called into question for the same conspiratorial reasons, and Malik Beasley. 
The NBA knows how bad a look this is for a league now so deeply connected with gaming partners, and these measures are a clear indication that it is trying, to whatever extent possible, to put the genie back in the bottle regarding the bets most ripe for manipulation.

schema.headline: NBA instructs sportsbook partners to ban certain bets ripe for manipulation, per report - CBS Sports

title: Serie A Matchweek 7: Can Inter, AS Roma, Como and Napoli recover after disastrous Champions League week? - CBS Sports

        Serie A is back this weekend after quite a challenging week of European soccer for the Italian teams, as all four clubs involved in the Champions League lost. Inter, the Serie A leaders, conceded four goals and lost to Club Brugge at San Siro. AS Roma led Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid 3-1 with 10 minutes to go before conceding three goals and losing 4-3 at the Stadio Olimpico on Wednesday. Napoli and Como also lost, so the only Italian wins of the week came from Juventus, AC Milan and Atalanta in the Europa League and Conference League. Let's now take a closer look at what to watch for on Matchday 7: the game, the player and the story you need to know.Game to watch: Juventus vs. LazioLazio have been the most surprising side of the Serie A season so far. Gennaro Gattuso's team is level with Inter at the top of the standings, with 16 points from five wins and a draw in the opening six matches. However, this weekend they will visit Juventus at the Allianz Stadium in Turin. Luciano Spalletti's side hasn't had a great start to the new season, with three wins, two draws and a defeat in its opening six games, and will be looking to react on Sunday after last weekend's draw at Cagliari. Gattuso has shown some encouraging signs following the disappointment of Italy's World Cup playoff elimination against Bosnia and Herzegovina earlier this year. Meanwhile, despite the ongoing boycott of home games by Lazio fans amid their dispute with club owner Claudio Lotito, the Biancocelesti continue to deliver consistent performances week after week.  Player to watch: Marcus ThuramAfter this week's home defeat to Club Brugge in the Champions League, Inter need to react immediately when they visit Bologna on Saturday. Inter coach Cristian Chivu will be without captain Lautaro Martinez for at least three weeks after the Argentinian striker suffered a muscular injury after the Champions League game. He won't be back until after the November international break, so he will also miss the Derby della Madonnina against AC Milan at San Siro on Oct. 31. Inter will now need to rely on their strikers Marcus Thuram, Ange-Yoan Bonny and Francesco Pio Esposito. In particular, the French international needs to step up in this phase to cope with the absence of Lautaro Martinez. It won't be easy by any means, but he's the one who has to make it happen.  Story of the weekend: Italians need a reactionIt was the first time in history that all four Italian teams lost on the same Champions League matchday. That makes it even more important for the four sides that suffered defeats in Europe this week to bounce back in their respective league fixtures. Inter have a challenging away game against Bologna, while Como will meet Fiorentina away as well. Napoli will take on Venezia, who just hired Davide Nicola to replace Giovanni Stroppa, on Saturday, while AS Roma will host their former captain and coach Daniele De Rossi, who is now in charge at Genoa.

title: Fantasy football Week 6 Start 'Em & Sit 'Em: Jalen Hurts out, Justin Herbert a risky start - CBS Sports

Fantasy football is about finding the right matchups. Week 6 is becoming one of the most difficult weeks of the season for lineup decisions. With four teams on bye, injuries piling up and several offenses struggling to find consistency Fantasy managers are being forced to make some choices. As we have already learned through five weeks, a player's name recognition or draft position does not always translate into a spot in your starting lineup.Take Jalen Hurts and Justin Herbert, for example. Both entered the season with Fantasy expectations but offensive struggles and difficult matchups make them tough to trust in Week 6. Meanwhile, players such as MarShawn Lloyd, Germie Bernard and Denzel Boston are emerging as intriguing starting options thanks to increased opportunities and favorable matchups.That is why looking beyond the box score is so important. Defensive schemes, pass-rush pressure, offensive line play and expected game scripts can make the difference between a Fantasy performance and a disappointing afternoon. Sometimes the smartest move is to sit a name in favor of a less‑established player with a clearer path to production.We will break down every Week 6 matchup. Identify the toughest start/sit decisions facing Fantasy managers. From players worth trusting to established stars who might belong on your bench, we'll examine matchups, opportunities and potential pitfalls to help you put together the strongest possible lineup.

Bo Nix has an average depth of target higher than 5.4 yards downfield in just one game -- Week 2 against the Jaguars (8.6) when he uncorked six throws of over 15 air yards, half to Jaylen Waddle. Jacksonville played a lot of man-to-man coverage in that matchup, and since then, the Broncos have seen just the eighth-fewest plays of man coverage against them. That trend will continue as the Seahawks are famously known for playing a ton of zone coverage under Mike Macdonald (they currently rank first at an 89.8% zone coverage rate) and they're also excellent at getting pressure on the quarterback without blitzing much. These are bad factors for Nix, who is struggling to throw downfield at all, let alone with efficiency. Jaylen Waddle doesn't have any good receiving metrics this season against zone coverage and doesn't even have an end zone target through five weeks -- it's really hard to trust him against the Seattle scheme. R.J. Harvey actually has the highest target-per-route rate among Broncos players this season, but didn't catch many passes in Week 5 because Denver stayed close and was able to run the ball. Woody Marks is expected to handle the majority of touches for the Texans, but it's against a Jaguars run defense that improved its rush yards allowed average to 2.5 last week against the Eagles' backups. Despite last week's heroics against the Titans, Marks is among the least efficient runners in the league, ranking bottom-10 among qualifiers in yards per rush (3.5), rush yards after contact (2.51), and rate of runs gaining zero/negative yards (27.9%). Unquestionably, some of this is due to his offensive line's woes, but it figures to hamper him against the Jaguars' defensive front. Marks will need to stay productive in the passing game to help in Fantasy, where he's been about league average this year. The Jaguars aren't quite as solid against running backs through the air, giving up a modest 6.6 yards per catch but missing on average more than two tackles per game against the position. Marks' workload, including his reception work, is solely what places him in the low-end No. 2 RB category.The Texans have the third-lowest blitz rate but are top-12 in pass rush pressure rate with or without a blitz. They're expected to lean into their pass rush, especially against the left side of the Jaguars offensive line, where veteran Walker Little takes over for injured starter Anton Harrison. Little had two of his worst games last year against the Texans, as did Trevor Lawrence, who has one career game over 19 Fantasy points against DeMeco Ryans' Texans defense. Lawrence has been really shaky when pressured this year, throwing a catchable ball at a low 61% rate (41.7% completion rate), with a much lower yards per attempt and QB rating compared to when he's not pressured. And when he is pressured, his targets are spread almost evenly, at least on a per-route basis, by Parker Washington, his peripheral receivers and his running backs, none of whom have impressive yard per route run rates in this specific situation. Had Lawrence fared better under pressure this year, he'd be a decent starter, but because he hasn't, and his track record isn't particularly good against the Texans, and the Texans themselves have been pretty good since faltering against Josh Allen in Week 1, it's probably worth considering benching Lawrence and lowering expectations for his other pass-catchers.

The Bears definitely tried to get Rome Odunze the ball against the Packers zone-heavy defense, but aggressive throws by Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum were broken up or intercepted (including four headed Odunze's way and two toward Colston Loveland). Moreover, the Bears ditched their quick-game pass attack, which is guaranteed to happen again this week with Caleb Williams back under center. Williams notoriously holds the ball a little too long and then scrambles to keep plays alive, sometimes with spectacular results, sometimes not. It's the primary reason why his best-known pass-catchers struggled in the first two weeks of the year -- plays designed for them went elsewhere because of Williams' tendencies. It's also why Kalif Raymond became a thing because he would frequently catch Williams' attention on those broken plays. The Falcons are a low-blitz, high pass-rush rate defense, exactly the kind that will send Williams' feet moving quickly. Williams' completion and catchable throw rates tumble when he's pressured. It's only been two games, but it's been Raymond who has, frankly, dominated per-route efficiency among Bears pass-catchers when Williams has been pressured or has faced zone coverage (which the Falcons play a lot of). Raymond is their third receiver, and his role hasn't really changed with Williams out, even though his targets have dwindled with Bagent and Keenum at QB. Atlanta has allowed 11-plus PPR points to two wide receivers in each of their past four games, seven of whom saw at least nine targets. Three separate times, a Bears receiver has had more than seven targets in a game this year, and just once (Raymond in Week 1) with Williams.MUST-START: Bijan Robinson, Drake LondonSTART: Caleb Williams, D'Andre Swift, Falcons DST (low-end start)FLEX: Luther Burden III, Rome Odunze,SIT: Michael Penix Jr., Kalif Raymond (bye-week WR), Kyle Pitts, Colston Loveland, Brian Robinson Jr. (bye-week RB), Jahan Dotson, Roschon Johnson (unless Swift misses time), Bears DST

The Ravens stay true to playing zone coverage without blitzing much. If there ever was a week for them to change that, it's this one: Deshaun Watson's passing metrics sink like a stone in Lake Erie when he sees man coverage, gets pressured or is against a one-high safety look. The Jets went blitz-heavy last week and sacked Watson eight times, something the Ravens should try to replicate. The man coverage will come on some third downs, and the pressure should be consistent versus a banged-up offensive line. Denzel Boston and Harold Fannin Jr. are two of five Browns players who see a target when Watson's pressured between 13% and 20% of their routes, and with poor efficiency (0.94 yards per route for Fannin, 0.47 for Boston). But it's the zone coverage where Boston has a fighting chance because he's been more effective (2.6 yards per route run), even if his target rate is a few percentage points behind Fannin's. With a pass-heavy game script on deck, not to mention a number of receivers hurt or on bye, Boston shapes up as at least a low-end No. 2 Fantasy WR, especially after coach Todd Monken said this week he wants Watson to get the ball out quicker.

If there was ever a get-right opponent for Daniel Jones, this is it. The zone-heavy Titans have mustered the second-lowest pass rush pressure rate this season at 26.8%, dipping to 20% over their past two games. They don't blitz a lot and they're keen on playing with a single-high safety to better contain the run. Taylor will absolutely get plenty of work, but don't be surprised to see Jones do well off of play-action and perhaps overall against a defense that's let up at least 20 Fantasy points to three of the past four quarterbacks it's faced. Best of all, the single-high safety look has led Jones to target Josh Downs at nearly a 25% route run clip for 1.94 yards per route, both well ahead of Keenan Allen. There's no question that rookie David Bailey turned the corner (literally and figuratively) last week against the Browns, boosting the Jets' pass rush in a big way. The question is whether he can do it again versus a Patriots offensive line that found a way to limit Maxx Crosby's impact a week ago. I'd expect the Jets to lean into their blitz more, but I'm not convinced they'll dial up much man-to-man coverage outside of third down. They've played the second-most Cover-2 this year and have nearly played the same amount of Cover-3, making up just over half of their total defensive snaps. In those specific situations, we could see Maye take downfield shots to Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams, with Chism a target per route leader against Cover-2 and Cover-1 (their third-most-used scheme and their most-used man-to-man scheme). Williams hasn't run enough routes to be considered for Fantasy, but Chism carries value as a high-floor PPR flex, as does Hunter Henry, who has come alive over the past two weeks as a middle-field winner from Maye. MUST-START: Garrett WilsonSTART: Drake Maye, Rhamondre Stevenson, Braelon Allen, Patriots DSTFLEX: Efton Chism III (low-end PPR flex), Romeo Doubs (low-end flex)SIT: Geno Smith, Hunter Henry (bye-week TE), Demario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Eli Raridon, Mason Taylor, Jets DST

New Orleans' defense couldn't get off the field last week, struggling to apply quick pass rush pressure on Kyler Murray and then failing to wrap him up before he scampered away or threw downfield. Jameis Winston isn't a runner, but he has been pretty decent at evading the pass rush and late last week unlocked the offense when they went into more no-huddle work in the fourth quarter. Malik Nabers has crushed the past two weeks on a huge 33.3% target share (Isaiah Likely's 30.9% isn't bad either) and should shine versus the heavy Cover-3 shell the Saints deploy. With time to throw and a solid-but-not-studly Saints secondary, I suspect Winston can take advantage of his third straight favorable matchup in a row. It's that Saints defense that allowed the Vikings to control the clock last week, limiting Tyler Shough and the Saints offense to just over 20 minutes and a season-low 43 plays (their previous low was 64 plays). 
Tyler Shough and the Saints offense were limited to just over 20 minutes and a season-low 43 plays (their previous low was 64 plays) last week. They should be in better position to get more plays this week, but there's evidence that the Giants defense is improving. They've blitzed at the second-highest rate in the two games since Brian Burns' injury, paying off last week with five sacks. When they blitz Shough, they won't just be following in the Vikings' footsteps but in the Falcons' too -- each of Shough's past two opponents came after him, and both kept him under 18 Fantasy points. Shough's passing numbers against pass rush pressure have faded to a 52.1% completion rate for 6.0 yards per attempt, two touchdowns, and a 70% catchable throw rate, all awful compared to when he's not pressured. And, Shough's rushing has withered over his past two games, perhaps because he doesn't want to aggravate a "banged up" left hand injury. I'd hesitate using Shough this week, and I might lower expectations a bit for Chris Olave also since his best numbers might only come when Shough isn't pressured, which has been the case on just 58% of his dropbacks since left tackle Kelvin Banks got hurt.MUST-START: Malik Nabers, Chris OlaveSTART: Jameis Winston, Isaiah Likely, Cam Skattebo, Juwan JohnsonFLEX: Devaughn Vele, Alvin Kamara (low-end PPR flex)SIT: Tyler Shough (bye-week QB), Kendre Miller (bye-week RB), Darnell Mooney, Noah Fant, Giants DST, Saints DST

Much has been made of Philadelphia's struggling offense, and with Jalen Hurts ruled out for Week 6, the Eagles face even more uncertainty heading into their matchup with Carolina. Their pass defense hasn't been particularly impressive, either. Their once-ferocious pass rush has just six sacks through five games, and their 32.8% pass-rush pressure rate isn't helped by their low blitz rate. Bryce Young's worst moments this season have come when he's been pressured, but that might not happen too often this week, especially if right tackle Taylor Moton returns to fortify a rested offensive line. It also helps Young that the Eagles tend to play a defensive style similar to the Panthers unit he practices against, right down to the heavy Cover-3 look. Jalen Coker has led the Panthers with a 30.8% target-per-route-run rate and a ridiculous 4.46 yards per route run against Cover-3 (Tetairoa McMillan has a strong 21.6% rate and 2.51 yards per route average as well). I would expect them to take turns lining up away from top Eagles cornerback Quinyon Mitchell, who has played to the quarterback's left nearly all season. With Hurts sidelined, Philadelphia's offense could struggle to sustain drives, potentially creating additional opportunities for Carolina's playmakers.A review of Tanner McKee's preseason film -- 58 dropbacks in Sean Mannion's offense -- shows him as a competent processor of coverage but perhaps a little too gunshy to aggressively throw downfield. McKee ran the quick-game passing offense, got through reads quickly, was willing to move his feet, rarely held the ball too long and would throw to easily defined one-on-one situations when he had the time. However, McKee was definitely too willing to get the ball out quickly to short-area targets, was affected by pass rush pressure, didn't throw with velocity often and was off-target frequently when he did. The Panthers typically play a ton of Cover-3 (single-high safety), but their pass rush pressure rate got significantly better versus the Browns and Lions offensive lines in Weeks 3 and 4. They'll be rested and ready to play against an Eagles O-line down at least three starters from Week 1. So even though McKee had time on the field this preseason with Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele, it's tough to buy into him connecting with them or anyone else for massive gains, even DeVonta Smith. Maybe the best hope is for McKee to throw a bunch of short targets to Lemon, Dallas Goedert and the running backs -- players with a low average depth of target.

The Buccaneers have settled into a heavy zone coverage unit, often with a single-high safety, blitzing at the NFL's third-highest rate but struggling to do anything with it. Todd Bowles' bunch has zero sacks in their past two games, six on the season, and just a 27% pass rush pressure rate. This lack of a pass rush has had a weird effect -- quarterbacks are comfortable but only one QB has over 20 Fantasy points against the Bucs this year, and it was Deshaun Watson. Everyone else has been below 17.1 Fantasy points, including Dak Prescott, who threw 42 times and Joe Burrow, who threw 35 times. I know Germie Bernard got a real opportunity last week, and I don't love chasing rookie numbers, but he actually leads the Steelers pass-catchers in per-route target data against the blitz and is just as targeted on a per-route basis against single-high coverage as DK Metcalf. It's been clear this year that Metcalf tends to see a good dose of targets against single-high coverage, but as a slot receiver, Bernard should be in the act as well. MUST-START: Jaylen Warren, Bucky Irving,START: Emeka Egbuka, DK Metcalf, Pat Freiermuth (low-end TE), Steelers DSTFLEX: Germie BernardSIT: Aaron Rodgers (high-end No. 2 QB), Jalon Daniels, Chris Godwin, Cade Otton, Ted Hurst, Tez Johnson, Darnell Washington, Kenneth Gainwell, Buccaneers DST (bye-week DST)

L.A.'s defense struggled against the Bills' run game on Monday, but it's a tough sell that the Cardinals will take advantage. The Rams previously held the Giants, Broncos and Eagles (with Saquon Barkley for much of the game) to under four yards per rush each, so it's not like they're terrible. Filtering out garbage time stats, the Cards are below league average in a bunch of categories, including rush EPA, RB rush yards per game (3.6), and rush yards before and after contact, plus they're in the bottom five in explosive rush rate with just three runs of 12-plus yards. Their beat-up offensive line and banged-up rookie rusher, whose snaps are being managed, are huge factors. They've also averaged 18.5 running back runs (excluding garbage time) over their four losses. The most likely game script is that the Rams build a lead on the Cardinals' weak defense and thus force Jacoby Brissett to throw at least 35 times, which he's done in 4 of 5 games this year and in both games against the Rams in 2025.Tyler Allgeier is a borderline start based on volume (he's averaged more PPR points per touch than Love this season anyway).  MUST-START: Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, Kyren Williams, Trey McBride, Davante AdamsSTART: Michael Wilson, Tyler Allgeier (low-end No. 2 PPR RB), Tyler HigbeeFLEX: Kendrick Bourne (PPR flex)SIT: Jacoby Brissett (bye-week QB), Bam Knight, Rams DST, Cardinals DST

The first thing to know before you consider starting any Chargers running back is that the Chiefs run defense held the Colts, Dolphins and Raiders to 3.5 or fewer yards per rush each in their past three games. Of the collective 72 rushes those running backs had, 21 of them went for zero or negative yards. That's nearly 30% of all runs, the best mark among NFL defenses in that span. Only three touchdowns were scored, two by Jonathan Taylor, including one from 24 yards out. This is a nightmare matchup for a Chargers offense expected to play behind on the scoreboard with a depleted offensive line (though they may have found something in the run game in rookie tackle Travis Burke). The second thing to know is that the Chargers used three RBs almost equally in their past two games. Omarion Hampton has played the lowest percentage of snaps among the three but got the most touches each week (at least 11 per game). However, if you go off the film, it's Kimani Vidal who's had more impressive runs and played with a little more physicality than Hampton as of late, and Keaton Mitchell is still delivering in the passing game. When asked about Hampton's decreasing snaps this week, coach Jim Harbaugh said he was "fired up" whenever Hampton was on the field, then went out of his way to praise Vidal before mentioning Mitchell. You can't help but wonder if Vidal picks up more than single-digit touches given his improved play compared to Hampton. Between that and the matchup, it makes me nervous to start any of them in Fantasy.
After Rashee Rice came up gimpy following a reception very early on in Week 4, the Chiefs effectively had Jalen Royals replace Rice's snaps but it was Tyquan Thornton and Xavier Worthy who saw the most targets -- eight for Thornton and seven for Worthy, but Thornton left Week 4's game with a severe injury and is out for a long while. The knee-jerk reaction is to assume the Chiefs will lean on Travis Kelce and Worthy as their top options in the passing game; no one from Andy Reid to Patrick Mahomes to even offensive coordinator Eric Bienemy offered insight on any of the other Chiefs wideouts. That's because the Chiefs are deliberate with how they bring along their receivers, which is why they might have been fine having Royals play a lot in their last game but not see many targets (just two, neither of which were first-read throws, despite a 64% route rate). If he's going to continue seeing targets then a stat line like what we saw in Week 4 or even Week 2 is certainly in play.
